answer: One operator can spin many keys that share a funding cluster. Admission uses a two-face core-split: the applicant cuts a 120 mm shale core from a published knoll grid cell (one cell per cluster per epoch) and sets a quartz shard whose facet encodes H(pubkey||cell||epoch) within 0.5 deg. Face B stays with a random established custodian for 9 hours. Cost is 95 locked units plus the cell. Three peers re-measure the facet and match both fracture maps. A wrong angle, early unseal, or mismatch burns 30 units and voids it; a reused cell or second miss empties the lock and bars the key for 14 epochs.
